hints: First order the 10 data values from smallest to largest.
For an even number of data values ($n = 10$), the median is the mean of the 5th and 6th values.
Find the lower quartile $Q_1$ (median of the lower 5 values) and upper quartile $Q_3$ (median of the upper 5 values).
Calculate the interquartile range using $IQR = Q_3 - Q_1$.
walkthrough:
Arrange the $n = 10$ values in ascending order:
$$36, \quad 37, \quad 38, \quad 38, \quad 38, \quad 39, \quad 40, \quad 40, \quad 42, \quad 45$$

Find the median as the midpoint of the 5th and 6th values:
$$\text{Median} = \dfrac{38 + 39}{2} = 38.5\text{ cm}$$

Determine the lower quartile $Q_1$ and upper quartile $Q_3$:
$$\begin{aligned} Q_1 &= \text{3rd value} = 38\text{ cm} \\ Q_3 &= \text{8th value} = 40\text{ cm} \end{aligned}$$

Compute the interquartile range ($IQR$):
$$IQR = Q_3 - Q_1 = 40 - 38 = 2\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.Finding Medians and Quartiles: Order the 10 values, calculate median as 38.5, identify Q1 = 38 and Q3 = 40, and find IQR = 2.

teacher_walkthrough:
To find the median and quartiles, we begin by placing the 10 data points in ascending order:
$$36, \quad 37, \quad 38, \quad 38, \quad 38, \quad 39, \quad 40, \quad 40, \quad 42, \quad 45$$

Step 1: Calculate the median.
Since $n = 10$ is even, the median lies halfway between the $\frac{10}{2} = 5$th value and the $6$th value:
- 5th value $= 38$
- 6th value $= 39$
$$\text{Median} = \frac{38 + 39}{2} = \frac{77}{2} = 38.5\text{ cm}$$

Step 2: Find the lower quartile ($Q_1$) and upper quartile ($Q_3$).
The median splits the 10 values into two equal halves of 5 values each:
- Lower half: $36, 37, 38, 38, 38$. The middle (3rd) value is $Q_1 = 38$.
- Upper half: $39, 40, 40, 42, 45$. The middle (8th) value is $Q_3 = 40$.

Step 3: Calculate the Interquartile Range ($IQR$):
$$IQR = Q_3 - Q_1 = 40 - 38 = 2\text{ cm}$$
Therefore, the median is $38.5$ cm and the interquartile range is $2$ cm.
